content.title: Metadata Is Part of the Application
content.hook: A page is not only what appears inside the visible body.
goals: Master Metadata Is Part of the Application: Put information near the boundary that owns it.

content.title: Why this matters
content.text:
Metadata can affect what users see in browser tabs, search-related contexts, and shared page information.

It is part of the page's identity.

content.question: Which title better communicates a product page?

content.title: Metadata should follow the route
content.text:
A dashboard layout might have application-level metadata.

A product detail route can provide more specific metadata.

The same principle appears again:

**Put information near the boundary that owns it.**

content.title: Dynamic metadata
content.text:
Some pages need metadata based on the current resource.

For example, a product page may need its title to include the product name.

That means metadata can participate in the same server-side data flow as the page.

content.question: Why should metadata be treated as application content?

options.text: Because it is unrelated to the page.
Because it communicates important page identity and context outside the visible body.

feedback.correct: Correct answer: B. Because it communicates important page identity and context outside the visible body.
feedback.incorrect: Correct answer: B. Because it communicates important page identity and context outside the visible body.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: Professional frontend work includes what users do not always see directly.
Metadata, loading states, errors, and structure are all part of the application experience.
nextSteps: Write the metadata you would use for a `/dashboard/reports` route and a `/products/42` route.

Complete the checkpoint and explain the mechanism in your own words. A wrong first prediction is expected; the mastery signal is whether you can explain the result and handle a changed case after feedback.
